Chapter 13: The Ongoing Struggle—Accepting the Absurd as a Way of Life
After all the searching, all the questions and struggles, there’s this gentle kind of acceptance that settles in.
It’s not about giving up or feeling defeated. Instead, it’s this quiet understanding that the absurd is just... part of our lives. The world isn’t going to hand us all the answers we want—and you know what? That’s actually okay.
Most of us don’t reach this place overnight. It’s a slow process, almost like peeling away old illusions, bit by bit, as we start to see things in a new light. The struggle with the absurd doesn’t feel so heavy anymore. In fact, it can start to feel like a companion—a gentle reminder that life is always going to be uncertain, unpredictable, and, honestly, pretty precious.
There’s a special kind of peace that comes with accepting the absurd. It means you stop clinging to the need for certainty, or expecting life to offer perfect guarantees and answers. Instead, you learn to live with your eyes—and your heart—wide open, ready to embrace all the messiness that being human brings.
The struggle itself doesn’t go away, but it changes. It becomes part of how you experience being alive, a way to find meaning just by living, day to day.
Sure, the world may stay silent, but that doesn’t mean we have to be. Our voices, our actions, our choices—they all matter, probably more than we realize.
And as another day winds down, when everything feels a little quieter, that struggle with the absurd is still there. But so is the possibility—the possibility of joy, of real connection, of finding meaning in even the smallest moments.
Maybe the search for answers never really ends. But sometimes, just searching—just showing up and living—is more than enough.
